name: Li-ion Battery Separators & Cell Materials Localisation
scope: Indian listed companies localising Li-ion cell materials (separator film, anode, cathode, electrolyte/LiPF6, binder, foil) as domestic ACC gigafactories start up, plus the policy, customers, valuation and risks around them.

summary.one_line: Nothing new on the materials projects this week, but the stock-performance data changes the picture. TCPL Packaging, the only listed separator-film entrant we could confirm, is up about 60% in six months. It has re-rated even though it has no named partner or customer and production is still targeted for Q4 FY28. Indian cell demand remains thin outside Exide's new 6 GWh plant.
key_points: TCPL Packaging's Rs 125 cr separator project is unchanged: 70 mn sq m a year (about 6-8 GWh of cells), funded by internal accruals and debt, with commercial production targeted for Q4 FY28 and a 500 mn sq m (about 50 GWh) ambition over 5-7 years. Phase 1 is coating and conversion of bought-in base film, and no technology partner or customer has been named (S1, S2). TCPL Energy Materials Ltd was incorporated on 24 Sep and there have been no project filings since (S3).

New this week: the 'barely covered' separator leg has already moved. Anand Rathi data shows TCPL up 60.1% over 6 months and 36.9% over 3 months, but only 17.5% over 1 year (S4). On screener.in it still trades at 29.2x trailing P/E, the lowest in the group (S3).

The anode and electrolyte names also re-rated over 6 months: Himadri +40.6%, Gujarat Fluorochemicals +33.7% and Graphite India +24.8%. Over the past month Himadri (-1.6%) and GFL (-5.1%) have cooled (S14, S17, S20). Trailing P/Es are 41.7x, 79.0x and 71.5x (S13, S16, S19).

Supply is still concentrated in China, which makes 74% of separators, 82% of electrolytes and 85% of anodes (2022, CSIS citing IEA) (S9). SBI's April 2026 sector report says over 60% of Indian battery material inputs come from China. Cathode, anode, electrolyte and separator materials make up about 70% of cell cost (S6).

Cell demand is the bottleneck. Exide commissioned 6 GWh on 23 Sep 2026 (S5). By Oct 2025 only 1.4 GWh had been commissioned under the ACC-PLI and no incentive had been paid out. Reliance has paused its cell plans after its Chinese technology talks collapsed (S23).

The component incentive (separator film, anode, cathode, electrolyte, copper foil) is still not approved. It is reported at up to Rs 13,000 cr and awaiting Expenditure Finance Committee approval (Business Today, Aug 2026; S7), or at about Rs 12,000 cr (ET via Outlook Business, Jun 2026; S8). We found no approval this week.

The battery businesses are still small. GFL's battery segment had revenue of Rs 14 cr and an EBITDA loss of Rs 30 cr in Q1 FY27, against group revenue of Rs 1,588 cr (S18). TCPL's first-phase revenue target of Rs 150-200 cr is about 9-11% of its FY26 revenue of Rs 1,763 cr (S2, S4; our arithmetic).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Materials makers whose domestic customers are commissioning now. Exide's 6 GWh Phase-I will first replace imported LFP cells in its own packs, with NMC and e-2W supply by the end of FY27 (S5). Amara Raja's 2 GWh Giga 1 is due in CY2027 (S24).
Anode makers named by ICICI Direct as likely winners from the component scheme: HEG and Graphite India, plus Hindalco for copper foil (S8).
If the scheme is approved, every material it covers would benefit, separator film included (S7).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Valuation has run ahead of earnings. TCPL is up 60% in 6 months with nothing to sell until FY28 (S2, S4). GFL trades at 79x P/E while its battery segment loses money (S18, S19).
Thin domestic demand: the PLI has been slow, Reliance has paused its cell plans and Ola's timelines have slipped (S23).
Chinese scale and policy: China's export controls on graphite anodes, cathode precursors and battery equipment were suspended for one year in Oct 2025, so they could come back around Nov 2026 (S25).
Qualification and execution for a packaging company entering a new process, with about a year of qualification planned (S2).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Q2 FY27 results in late Oct-Nov. Trading windows are closed at TCPL, Himadri, GFL and Graphite India (S3, S13, S16, S19). Watch TCPL for land, technology partner and equipment news (S1) and GFL for progress towards three-digit quarterly battery revenue by Q4 FY27 (S18).
Whether the Expenditure Finance Committee and Cabinet approve the component scheme (S7).
Whether China's export-control suspension lapses or is extended around Nov 2026 (S25).
Himadri's LFP cathode Phase-I in Q3 FY27 (S11) and HEG/TACC's Dewas anode plant in Q1 CY2027 (S22).

subsections.title: What a separator is and how much India will need

blocks.text: A separator is a thin, porous polyolefin film between a cell's anode and cathode. It stops short circuits while letting ions flow, and ceramic-coated variants improve thermal stability (S6). TCPL describes the wet process it plans to use: polyethylene granules and additives are blended and extruded, the film is stretched, pores are formed by solvent extraction, and the film is then coated, slit, wound and tested. Separators are about 4-6% of cell cost (S1). ResearchAndMarkets values the global market at USD 8.0 bn in 2025 and forecasts USD 17.14 bn by 2031, a 13.54% CAGR. APAC holds about 55%, and demand is shifting to coated and multilayer separators (S10).

TCPL cites Ministry of Heavy Industries data showing Indian battery demand rising from 0.5 GWh in 2020 to 255.7 GWh in 2035 (S1). SBI expects about 180 GWh of cumulative demand by 2030 (S6). TCPL's own ratio is 70 mn sq m for 6-8 GWh, or roughly 9-12 mn sq m per GWh (S1). On that ratio, 255.7 GWh would need around 2.2-3.0 bn sq m a year, and Exide's 6 GWh alone would need about 50-70 mn sq m, roughly the size of TCPL's whole first phase. These figures are our arithmetic, not company estimates.

blocks.caption: Share of global Li-ion component production (2022)

blocks.text: The CSIS shares come from different IEA tables and are not internally consistent: China plus Japan comes to more than 100% for separators. They are shown as published (S9). The leading separator suppliers are SEMCORP (China), Asahi Kasei (Japan), SK Group (Korea) and W-SCOPE (S10). In India, SBI says the country has no upstream production of cathode, anode, electrolyte or separator materials and sources over 60% of material inputs from China (S6). Cell plants also depend fully on imported equipment, with a 10 GWh plant costing Rs 4,500-6,000 cr (S6).

items: ACC-PLI: Rs 18,100 cr for 50 GWh, of which 40 GWh has been awarded (S1, S7). The scheme targeted 50 GWh by Dec 2024. By Oct 2025 only 1.4 GWh had been commissioned, from one company, and no incentive had been disbursed (IEEFA via AMS; S23).

Proposed component scheme covering anode and cathode active materials, electrolytes, separator film and copper foil. Business Today reported up to Rs 13,000 cr on 27 Aug 2026, with inter-ministerial consultation complete and Expenditure Finance Committee approval pending (S7). ET, via Outlook Business, reported about Rs 12,000 cr on 18 Jun 2026, with incentives conditioned on real local manufacturing and import-duty relief still undecided (S8). No disbursement timeline has been published.
A separate 10 GWh grid-storage ACC programme is also proposed (S1).

blocks.text: We found no approval of the component scheme as of 9 Oct 2026. TCPL's disclosed economics (Rs 150-200 cr of revenue and 'good double-digit' margins) are not presented as dependent on it (S2).

blocks.text: In Q1 FY27 TCPL reported total income of Rs 494.9 cr (+15.9%) and PAT of Rs 40.0 cr (+79.2%) (S2). FY26 revenue was Rs 1,763 cr and net profit was Rs 97 cr (S4). The separator plan runs from land, technology and equipment ordering in 2026, through construction and validation in 2027, to commercial production and customer qualification in early 2028 (S1). Management expects at least a year of qualification and testing before commercial supply (S2).

Credibility check: TCPL relies on its existing films and polymer-processing capability (S1). Its phase one is coating and conversion of sourced film, and it will make its own base film only if demand builds (S1, S2). No technology partner or customer has been named, and its exchange announcements since the 24 Sep subsidiary incorporation show nothing further on the project (S3).

items: Himadri: FY26 revenue Rs 4,660.7 cr and PAT Rs 755 cr. It commissioned its first anode material plant in Apr 2026 and targets LFP cathode Phase-I in Q3 FY27 (S11). The 200 MTPA anode plant uses in-house technology, against a 200,000 MT long-term ambition (S12). No customer qualification win has been disclosed in the sources reviewed.

Graphite India: a Rs 4,330 cr synthetic-graphite anode plan approved on 28 Jan 2026 (S15) and an MoU with Maharashtra (S8), against FY26 net profit of Rs 264 cr (S17). On 29 Sep the US set a preliminary dumping margin of 12.22% on its graphite electrodes, a headwind for the core business that has to fund the capex (S16).
HEG: its subsidiary TACC is building a 20,000 tpa synthetic graphite anode plant at Dewas, due in Q1 2027. A Mandideep demo line is running qualification trials with international cell makers (S22).
Gujarat Fluorochemicals: battery revenue of Rs 14 cr against Rs 1,588 cr for the group in Q1 FY27, under 1%. Funding for the Oman project, now moved to India, is still being raised (S18).

Neogen Chemicals: Q1 FY27 Neogen Ionics revenue of Rs 19 cr against FY27 guidance of Rs 300 cr, including Rs 100 cr of electrolyte for ACC-PLI cell makers (S21). AMS notes that Indian materials makers are largely selling overseas for lack of domestic cell demand (S23).

sections.title: Research house views and market pricing

blocks.caption: Returns (Anand Rathi) and valuation (screener.in), close of 8 Oct 2026

blocks.title: Share price returns to 8 Oct 2026
blocks.source: Source: Anand Rathi stock pages (S4, S14, S17, S20)

blocks.text: Anand Rathi's pages are internally inconsistent, and the summary text gives TCPL's 6-month return as 55.4% (S4). Screener.in's 1-year figures are close: TCPL 17%, Himadri 46%, Graphite India 36% and GFL 17% (S3, S13, S16, S19). The brief's 'GFL +43% in 6 months' is not current, since the 6-month return is now 33.7% (S20). The brief's view that the separator leg is the earliest and least priced holds on P/E but not on recent price momentum.

ICICI Direct's note on the component scheme names HEG, Graphite India and Hindalco as likely winners. It does not mention TCPL, Himadri or GFL (S8). SBI's CHAKRA project-finance unit identifies separators and cathode materials as India's key capability gaps (S6). We found no broker initiation that groups TCPL with the materials names. We also found no other listed Indian separator-film entrant: searches of BOPP/BOPET makers turned up nothing. The separator bucket is a single small cap, which reflects how early the niche is rather than a gap in our search.

items: Chinese scale: China makes 74% of separators and 82% of electrolytes (S9). Its Oct 2025 export controls on graphite anodes, cathode precursors and battery equipment were suspended for one year (S25). They cut both ways, protecting local anode makers while raising equipment and technology risk.
Demand slippage: only 1.4 GWh had been commissioned under the PLI by Oct 2025, Reliance has paused its cell plans and Ola has slipped (S23). Materials makers may have to export (S23).
Qualification: TCPL expects at least a year of qualification (S2), and GFL's battery EBITDA is still negative (S18).
Capex and leverage: Graphite India's Rs 4,330 cr is part debt-funded (S15), TACC uses about Rs 1,250 cr of SBI debt (S22), and GFL is still raising funds (S18).

Technology shift: CATL is building a 40 GWh sodium-ion facility backed by a 60 GWh order (S6). Sodium-ion would not need graphite anodes or LiPF6. The move to coated and multilayer separators (S10) raises the bar for a coating-first entrant.
Q2 FY27 results in late Oct-Nov, after trading windows reopen (S3, S13, S16, S19).
TCPL Energy Materials: land, technology partner and equipment orders, all due in 2026 (S1).
Cabinet approval of the component scheme (S7, S8).
China's export-control suspension expiring around Nov 2026 (S25).
Himadri LFP Phase-I in Q3 FY27 (S11); TACC Dewas in Q1 CY2027 (S22); Amara Raja Giga 1 in CY2027 (S24); Exide NMC and e-2W supply by end FY27 (S5).

companies.name: TCPL Packaging Ltd
companies.role: Folding-carton and films maker entering wet-process separator film through TCPL Energy Materials Ltd: Rs 125 cr, 70 mn sq m initial capacity (S1, S3).
companies.impact: Phase-1 revenue of Rs 150-200 cr from Q4 FY28 if qualification succeeds (S2). The stock is up 60% in 6 months to 29.2x P/E with no named partner or customer (S3, S4).

companies.name: Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd
companies.role: Coal-tar-pitch major that commissioned a 200 MTPA anode plant in Apr 2026 and is building LFP cathode capacity (S11, S12).
companies.impact: Up 43% over 1 year at 41.7x P/E (S13, S14). Battery output is still at pilot scale against a 200,000 MT ambition (S12).

companies.name: Graphite India Ltd
companies.role: Graphite-electrode maker with a Rs 4,330 cr synthetic graphite anode plan (S15); named by ICICI Direct as a likely scheme beneficiary (S8).
companies.impact: Capex is many times its FY26 net profit of Rs 264 cr (S17). The stock trades at 71.5x P/E, and a US preliminary dumping margin on electrodes adds pressure (S16).

companies.name: HEG Ltd
companies.role: Graphite-electrode maker whose subsidiary TACC is building a 20,000 tpa synthetic graphite anode plant at Dewas, with qualification trials under way (S22).
companies.impact: Named by ICICI Direct as a likely winner from anode incentives (S8). Commissioning in Q1 CY2027 is the test (S22).

companies.name: Gujarat Fluorochemicals Ltd
companies.role: Fluoropolymer major building LiPF6, electrolyte, PVDF binder, LFP and anode materials through GFCL EV (S18).
companies.impact: Battery revenue is under 1% of the group and loss-making (S18). The stock trades at 79.0x P/E after +33.7% over 6 months (S19, S20).

companies.name: Neogen Chemicals Ltd
companies.role: Electrolyte and lithium-salt maker through Neogen Ionics, with Mitsubishi and Morita partnerships (S21, S23).
companies.impact: Guides to Rs 300 cr of FY27 battery revenue, including Rs 100 cr of electrolyte for ACC-PLI cell makers (S21).

companies.name: Hindalco Industries Ltd
companies.role: Setting up battery-grade copper foil capacity (S8).
companies.impact: Copper foil is one of the five scheme-covered components, and China controls about 80% of global copper-foil capacity (S8).

companies.name: Exide Industries Ltd
companies.role: Cell maker through Exide Energy Solutions; 6 GWh Phase-I commissioned on 23 Sep 2026 (S5).
companies.impact: The first scaled domestic buyer of cell materials as it replaces imported cells (S5).

companies.name: Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Ltd
companies.role: 60 MWh qualification plant since Jul 2026; 2 GWh Giga 1 in CY2027 within a 16 GWh programme (S24).
companies.impact: A potential materials buyer from CY2027 (S24).

companies.name: Ola Electric Mobility Ltd
companies.role: ACC-PLI cell maker sourcing cathode from Umicore and anode from Epsilon (S23).
companies.impact: Timelines have slipped, which limits near-term domestic materials demand (S23).

companies.name: Reliance Industries Ltd
companies.role: ACC-PLI awardee whose cell plans are paused; now assembling BESS from imported components (S23).
companies.impact: Its pause removes a potential anchor buyer of local materials for now (S23).

method: 2026-W41 update, researched on 9 Oct 2026 with web search and page fetches. We re-fetched these W40 sources and confirmed them: TCPL (Packman, Multibagg), GFL Q1, CSIS and ResearchAndMarkets. Other W40 company sources (Exide, Himadri, Graphite India, Neogen, Amara Raja, Business Today) were carried forward from last week's fetches. Market data was refreshed from screener.in and Anand Rathi pages as of the 8 Oct 2026 close; Anand Rathi provides the 1-, 6- and 12-month returns that W40 could not confirm. New this week: the SBI sector report, the ICICI Direct scheme note via Outlook Business, AMS on PLI slippage and the Reliance pause, HEG/TACC added to the universe, and the timing of China's export-control suspension. Dropped as stale or unconfirmed: W40's 30 Sep valuations, the Hindalco aluminium-foil item (replaced by copper foil per ICICI Direct), and the Ola 6 GWh scale-up claim. Searches for October 2026 filings on scheme approval or new separator entrants (including BOPP/BOPET film makers) found nothing. No ratings or price targets are given.
